name: Cefpirome

overview.mechanism: A beta-lactam antibacterial that inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis.
uses: Treatment of susceptible bacterial infections; select the indication and regimen from the current product insert and microbiology.

paragraphs.text: In a study of 22 patients, cefpirome clearance tracked creatinine clearance, and elimination half-life increased as renal function declined. Reduced renal elimination can substantially increase exposure.

Cefpirome is mainly recovered unchanged in urine. Historical renal-PK findings do not provide a universal modern HD or CRRT regimen; renal replacement settings and pathogen susceptibility require separate assessment.

The 1993 pharmacokinetic review reports approximately 10% protein binding and distribution resembling extracellular fluid. These are descriptive pharmacokinetic properties, not a validated dialysis dose.

sources.citation: Lameire et al. Single-dose pharmacokinetics of cefpirome in patients with renal impairment. Clin Pharmacol Ther. 1992;52:24–30. PubMed PMID: 1623690.
